cards.text: Israel's on the plains of Moab, and the LORD has said the land will be divided among the tribes (Numbers 26:3, 53). Now meet five sisters from the clans of Manasseh: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah. They're the daughters of Zelophehad, and friend, they are about to walk up and say something.

cards.question: The five daughters of Zelophehad go to make their case. Where do they go?

answers.text: To the entrance to the Tent of Meeting
To the gate of the city
To the foot of Mount Sinai

cards.text: They stand before Moses, Israel's leader, Eleazar the priest, the leaders AND the whole congregation. That's not asking your boss for a raise, friend, that's asking at the company-wide meeting with the microphone ON.
The sisters start with their dad: he died in the wilderness, and he had no sons. Then they clear something up about how he died.

cards.question: The daughters of Zelophehad say their father was among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD.
Zelophehad wasn't with Korah's followers. His daughters say he died because of his own ___.

cards.text: Then they ask, "Why should the name of our father disappear from his clan because he had no sons?" Friend, that's not a question. That's a closing argument.

cards.question: The land is about to be divided up. So what do the daughters of Zelophehad ask for?
Five sisters just asked Moses, in front of everyone, for property. What does Moses do with their case?

answers.text: He brings it before the LORD
He hands it to the leaders

cards.text: And the LORD answers him. Five sisters, one question, and now God Himself is weighing in. Ohhh, baker, it is getting GOOD.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses that the daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly.
The LORD tells Moses to give the sisters property and transfer their father's ___ to them.

cards.text: That's not a maybe, friend. That's a "You certainly must," and then the LORD tells Moses to say a new rule to all the Israelites.

cards.question: Under the LORD's new rule for Israel, if a man dies and leaves no son, who gets his inheritance?
If the man leaves no son and no daughter, his inheritance goes to his ___.

cards.text: No brothers either? Then it goes to his father's brothers. The LORD has thought of EVERY branch on this family tree.

cards.question: If the man's father has no brothers either, the LORD says the inheritance goes to another tribe.

cards.text: It goes to the next of kin from his clan, and the LORD makes it a statutory ordinance for the Israelites. Five sisters ask one question and it becomes the law, while I spent YEARS in a junk drawer and the only rule with my name on it was "Don't touch Dorin, he's sticky."

findings.problem: Korah appears for the first time in this lesson on this card, and nothing says who he is. A baker who doesn't know Numbers 16 can't make sense of the statement. Add a short line saying who he is, such as the Levite who led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16:1-3), without hinting whether Zelophehad was among his followers.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "The land is about to be divided up" adds a time the text doesn't give. Numbers 26:53 says the land will be apportioned. It doesn't say this is about to happen, and the dividing comes much later, after the Jordan crossing. Say it plainly instead, for example "The land will be divided up."

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new detail in Papa Dorin's backstory: a rule in the Millers' kitchen or the drawer saying "Don't touch Dorin, he's sticky." That is not in his story. Jokes may make up small moments and habits only around his bakery, not new facts about the Millers' kitchen or the junk drawer. Rework the joke so it uses only his established backstory or a bakery moment.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
